question: Does the experimental CUDA backend (backend 2 of the research coarse/frame API: exact device pyramid, one fused coarse launch over all angles with sparse peak entries, Q28-guarded fine search with __dp4a stripes) return matches bit-identical to the same build's CPU backend on Windows x86-64, and how does it change the per-frame time (prepare + match) of the 17 fixtures on the RTX PRO 4000?
sources: git archive of each commit's cpp-core (docs excluded), unpacked into fresh directories

pc.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, compute capability 12.0, 70 SMs, 24 GB, driver 596.71, WDDM, no display attached
pc.toolchain: MSVC 19.44.35207, CUDA 13.2 Update 2 (nvcc V13.2.86, MD5 of cuda_13.2.2_windows.exe 9e4bcad21f296561fa834a4eeda079d2 as published), CMake 3.31.6, Ninja, Release, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120, nvcc -fmad=false -lineinfo, static cudart

builds.after-cuda: 9623880 with FPM_BUILD_EXPERIMENTS=ON FPM_WITH_CUDA=ON (every timing and identity arm runs this one build's fpm_frame_bench)
builds.core-base / core-after: c67ca33 and 9623880 pure core (fpm_c.dll) for the core identity gate

pc.affinity: drivers start with `start /affinity C03C02` (P-cores 1,10-13,22,23); children inherit it

mac.host: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GiB, Apple clang 21
mac.builds: 9623880 pure core and research build (GUI, OpenCV, experiments; no CUDA), and c67ca33 pure core

inputs: the 17 compare_versions cases as 8-bit PGM copies from export_fixture_pgm.py; manifest.json sha256 3a539fec058b4f42e613c074a8fcb0f697ae2ca671cd76645bc8a23b6cd8e64f, checked on the PC before any run

arms.cpu: fpm_frame_bench backend 0: CPU pyramid, coarse and fine search (the matcher's own CPU path)
arms.cuda_coarse: backend 2, CPU pyramid, device coarse search only (fine on CPU): the coarse stage's share

metric: per-frame time = fpm_frame_prepare (source copy and pyramid) + fpm_frame_match, image decoding and frame/pattern creation excluded; steady = median of 5 calls after 500 ms of untimed calls in the same process; cold = that process's first call. Backend device times, sync counts and FP64 pixel counts are diagnostics only.

gates.ctest: the PC after-cuda build passes ctest with experimental_cuda_backend and experimental_cuda_kernels run (not skipped); on the Mac, 9623880 passes the pure core ctest and the research build ctest
gates.identity: every run of every arm (timing rounds and identity-only runs) returns matches bit-identical to the cpu arm of the same round, case and mode; zero mismatches and zero failed runs
gates.core_unchanged: check_backend_identity.py with fpm_c of c67ca33 and 9623880 on the PC (--pgm-dir) and on the Mac: zero differences (17 cases x 4 modes x SIMD/scalar)
gates.guard_exercised: fpm_cuda_kernel_test reports at least 4 poses where Q28 and binary64 round a pixel differently (each inside the guard) and nonzero FP64 pixels and FP64 maps
gates.mutants: cuda_mutants.py: 24 compiled mutants (23 in coarse_cuda.cu, 1 in selectPeaksSparse); all KILLED; the unmutated and restored trees pass

hypotheses.H1: steady geometric mean of cuda/cpu over the 17 cases is below 0.5 in each mode (exhaustive, fast, subpixel)
hypotheses.H2: at least 15 of the 17 cases are faster with cuda in each mode (predicted exception: Src9, the smallest case)
hypotheses.descriptive: cold first-call times, process peak RSS (expected higher for cuda: CUDA context and page-locked buffers) and retained device bytes are reported, not gated

timing.tool: benchmark_frame_backend.py --rounds 8 --repeat 5 --warmup-ms 500 (round 0 kept but left out of the summary), arms cpu, cuda, cuda_coarse; arm order alternates by round; fresh process per run
timing.identity_only_run: benchmark_frame_backend.py --rounds 2 --repeat 1 --warmup-ms 0 with arms cpu, cuda_unfused, cuda_batch8, cuda_cpu_pyramid
timing.quiet: nothing else runs on the PC during the timing runs; mutants and profiling run afterwards
timing.no_drops: no run is dropped or repeated; a failed run is reported as failed

decision_rule: The backend is kept as an opt-in research backend when every gate passes. H1 and H2 are reported as measured; a failure is disclosed, not tuned away. Defaults do not change.
not_formal: cuda_pilot.cu (exactness and latency pilot), the exploratory runs explore1/explore2 and the nsys/ncu profiles of uncommitted trees chose the design (FP64 warp to Q28 guard, dp4a stripes, two blocks per SM, template reuse) and are archived as selection evidence only
profiling: Nsight Systems (--trace=cuda,nvtx,wddm) and Nsight Compute runs of 9623880 are made after the formal runs, separately; their times are not formal
